Read the suppression lists of the mail service, whole

suppression_read.Rd

It only reads. A GET on each of the five lists of suppression_lists(), page by page, with a key whose only rights are those reads: no /mail/send, no DELETE. Taking an address off a list is a gesture IT makes by hand in the console, after correcting what made it bounce (decided on 2026-11-12). A guard in test-runner-guardie.R holds this function to that.

Usage

suppression_read(api_key, limit = 500L, max_pages = 200L)

Arguments

api_key

The read-only key, which the runner reads from Key Vault.

limit

Entries per page.

max_pages

Pages per list, the empty one included, past which the list is taken as one that never ends. Bounces held a few hundred entries in November 2026: 200 pages are 100.000 entries at 500 a page, 20.000 at 100.

Value

A list with ok, errors and voci, a data frame of lista, email, creata (POSIXct, UTC) and motivo, every entry of the five lists when ok, none otherwise.

Details

The key goes in the Authorization header and nowhere else, as in mail_send(). A failure is an outcome and not an exception, with the service's own words on the standard error, which is the journal of the unit: on 2026-08-27 the same refusal by IP Access Management answered 403 on one endpoint and 401 on another.

Each request waits thirty seconds at most, and a time out is a failure like any other: the reading comes before the report, and must not hold it.

The first failure stops the reading: a list read in part is not a list read, and nothing that follows would change that. A failure on the first page of a list is TRASPORTO_SOPPRESSIONI_NON_LEGGIBILI (the network, a key refused or revoked, an address not admitted); a failure on a later page, or a list that never ends, is TRASPORTO_SOPPRESSIONI_INCOMPLETE. The list ends at the first page that comes back empty, and not at the first shorter than limit: the ceiling per page is the documentation's and not measured, and a service that hands back fewer entries than asked would otherwise close the list after its first page with the reading said whole. One request more per list, five a day. The next page starts after the entries received, not after limit. A list that reaches max_pages without an empty page is a reading that failed, not a list cut short.

The parameters limit and offset, the ceiling of 500 entries per page and the shape of an entry (email, created in seconds since the epoch, reason where the list has one) are those of SendGrid's documentation of the v3 API as read on 2026-11-12, not yet measured: the first reading on the machine says whether the service agrees.
